cases.question: How many plumbin requests are waiting_part?
cases.title: Plumbing requests waiting for parts
cases.sql: select count(*) as plumbing_requests_waiting_parts from maintenance where category='plumbing' and state='waiting_parts'
assumptions: Counts all such requests regardless of date or priority

cases.question: Show open electricle maintenance requests with their unit.
cases.title: Open electrical maintenance requests with unit
cases.sql:
SELECT m.request_id AS "Request", m.opened AS "Opened", m.priority AS "Priority", m.state AS "Status", b.name AS "Building", u.unit_number AS "Unit", u.unit_type AS "Unit type", m.assigned_to AS "Assigned staff", m.cost AS "Cost"
FROM maintenance m
JOIN unit u ON u.unit_id = m.unit_id
JOIN building b ON b.building_id = u.building_id
WHERE m.category = 'electrical' AND m.state = 'open'
ORDER BY m.opened
assumptions: 'Open' means requests whose status is exactly 'open'; requests that are in progress or waiting for parts are not included.
The unit is shown by its building name and unit number.

Check: The report treats "open" as only the exact status 'open', so electrical requests that are in progress or waiting for parts are left out, even though a business user would usually count them as still open. Check whether those statuses should be included before relying on the 5 rows.
